note: HQ.1. A heritage base binds a type, never a namespace. TeamDomainObject.cs declares the file-scoped namespace Shop.Teams.DomainObject, whose PACKAGE sits in the file's symbol table under its last segment `DomainObject`, so `TeamDomainObject : DomainObject<Team>` bound that PACKAGE (rule module_symbol, fact) instead of the generic base class Shop.Core.Commands.DomainObject<T>; `Initial : Migration` (EF Core's base, outside the repo) bound the one PACKAGE named Migration, Shop.Contents.Migration (rule global_unique, heuristic). Baseline HEAD 1a33f0e8 (debug CLI): both forbids fire and the exact expect misses (`implementors TeamDomainObject --up` -> PACKAGE Shop::Teams::DomainObject; `implementors Initial --up` -> PACKAGE Shop::Contents::Migration).

expect_edges.note: the generic base class, the one non-namespace node named DomainObject (rule global_unique); exact, since the lenient matcher would also accept the PACKAGE of that name
positive control: a base the file itself declares still binds through the file's symbols (rule module_symbol)

forbid.note: the class's own namespace PACKAGE is no supertype
